\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Smooth Variation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.SmoothVariation
\section{Overview}
Positive-angle rotation quotients recover directional derivatives. Gaussian directional moments and nonnegative integral bounds then control Euclidean gradient length by normalized rotation variation, allowing infinite bounds.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative along a Gaussian rotation curve]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianRotation_comp}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative $L$ at $x\in\mathbb R^n$, and let $y\in\mathbb R^n$. Then $\theta\mapsto f(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)$ has derivative $L(y)$ at zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Limit of absolute rotation quotients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianRotation_difference_quotient_tendsto}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianRotation_comp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative $L$ at $x$, and let $y\in\mathbb R^n$. Then $|f(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)-f(x)|/\theta\to|L(y)|$ as $\theta\to0^+$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absolute Gaussian functional moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_gaussianLinearMap}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_gaussianProjection,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. For a linear functional $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, put $|L|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i L(e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ is the canonical basis. Then $\mathbb E|L(X)|=|L|_2\,2\varphi(0)$, where $\varphi$ is the one-dimensional standard Gaussian density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Directional integral from rotation variation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianRotation_derivative_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianRotation_difference_quotient_tendsto,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable everywhere with derivative $L(x)$, and put $|L(x)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i(L(x)e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ is the canonical basis. Let $C\in[0,\infty]$. If $\mathbb E(|f(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y)-f(X)|/\theta)\le C$ for every $\theta>0$, then $\mathbb E|L(X)Y|\le C$, with both expectations interpreted as nonnegative extended integrals.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of Gaussian linear functionals]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianLinearMap}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. Every continuous real linear functional $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is $\gamma_n$-integrable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegative absolute functional moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_abs_gaussianLinearMap}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianLinearMap,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_gaussianLinearMap,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. For a linear functional $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, put $|L|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i L(e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ is the canonical basis. The nonnegative extended expectation satisfies $\mathbb E|L(X)|=|L|_2\,2\varphi(0)$, with the finite expression on the right embedded into $[0,\infty]$ and $\varphi$ the standard Gaussian density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegative moment for a functional family]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianLinearMap_family}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_abs_gaussianLinearMap,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. If $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathcal L(\mathbb R^n,\mathbb R)$ is continuous, put $|L(x)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i(L(x)e_i)^2}$. Then $\mathbb E|L(X)Y|=(\mathbb E|L(X)|_2)\,2\varphi(0)$ as nonnegative extended integrals, where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gradient integral from normalized variation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianGradient_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_surface_normalization,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianLinearMap_family,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianRotation_derivative_le,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable everywhere with derivative $L(x)$, and put $|L(x)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i(L(x)e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ is the canonical basis. \end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gradient bound from real rotation integrals]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianGradient_le_of_integral_variation_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianGradient_le,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable everywhere with derivative $L(x)$, and put $|L(x)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i(L(x)e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ is the canonical basis. Assume $L$ is continuous, $0\le f\le1$, and $C\in[0,\infty]$. If $\sqrt{\pi/2}\,\mathbb E|f(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y)-f(X)|/\theta\le C$ for every $\theta>0$, where the real expectation is embedded into $[0,\infty]$, then the nonnegative extended expectation satisfies $\mathbb E|L(X)|_2\le C$.
\end{lemma}
